summary: @servicetitan/error-boundary ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated bundle
details: The package advertises itself as a React error boundary (dist/index.js is a 68-byte re-export) but package.json declares "preinstall": "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs downloads a Bun runtime binary from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/ into a temp directory, chmod +x's it, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun single-file compiled bundle (header `// @bun @bun-cjs`) with rotated string-array obfuscation and hex-mangled identifiers, with no source, sourcemap, README reference, or declared purpose. Fetching an alternate runtime at preinstall to execute an obfuscated bundle unrelated to the library's stated function is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern; the Bun-compiled payload frustrates Node-focused static analysis. Consumers installing the package by name receive automatic execution of attacker-controlled code on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
